title: Matthew Chapter 20 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Matthew chapter 20 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Matthew Chapter 20 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Matthew Chapter 20.

questions.question: In Matthew 20, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The householder went out early in the morning
The lord of the vineyard called the labourers
The first labourers were hired at the sixth hour
questions.correctAnswer: The householder went out early in the morning
questions.explanation: This event occurs first in the chapter as stated in Matthew 20:1.

questions.question: What did the householder agree to pay the labourers for a day's work?
questions.explanation: The householder agreed to pay a penny a day as stated in Matthew 20:2.

questions.question: At what hour did the householder first go out to hire more labourers?
questions.explanation: The householder went out at the third hour to hire more labourers as mentioned in Matthew 20:3.

questions.question: What did the householder promise the labourers he found at the third hour?
questions.explanation: He promised them whatever is right, as stated in Matthew 20:4.

questions.question: How many times did the householder go out to hire labourers?
questions.explanation: The householder went out five times, as he went out at the early morning, third hour, sixth hour, ninth hour, and eleventh hour as noted in Matthew 20:5 and Matthew 20:6.

questions.question: What reason did the last group of labourers give for standing idle?
questions.explanation: The last group stated that no man had hired them as recorded in Matthew 20:7.

questions.question: What instruction did the lord of the vineyard give regarding the payment of the labourers?
options: Pay the first and then the last
Begin from the last unto the first
Pay only those who worked all day
questions.correctAnswer: Begin from the last unto the first
questions.explanation: The lord instructed to pay beginning from the last hired to the first, as stated in Matthew 20:8.

questions.question: What did those hired at the eleventh hour receive?
questions.explanation: They received a penny each as mentioned in Matthew 20:9.

questions.question: What did the first labourers suppose they would receive?
questions.explanation: The first labourers supposed they would receive more, as indicated in Matthew 20:10.

questions.question: What did the first labourers do after receiving their pay?
questions.explanation: They murmured against the goodman of the house as stated in Matthew 20:11.

questions.question: What complaint did the first labourers make?
options: The last labourers only worked one hour
questions.correctAnswer: The last labourers only worked one hour
questions.explanation: They complained that the last labourers had only worked one hour and were treated equally, as noted in Matthew 20:12.

questions.question: The householder went out to hire labourers into his vineyard.
questions.explanation: This statement is true as it is explicitly stated in Matthew 20:1.

questions.question: The householder paid all labourers the same amount.
questions.explanation: This statement is true; all labourers received a penny regardless of their hours worked, as stated in Matthew 20:9.

questions.question: The labourers who worked all day received two pennies.
questions.explanation: This statement is false; the labourers who worked all day received only a penny, as indicated in Matthew 20:10.

questions.question: The householder hired labourers at the tenth hour.
questions.explanation: This statement is false; the householder went out at the eleventh hour, not the tenth hour, as noted in Matthew 20:6.

medium.title: Matthew Chapter 20 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Matthew Chapter 20 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What was the wage agreed upon for the laborers in the vineyard?
questions.explanation: This is stated in Matthew 20:2, where it mentions that the householder agreed with the laborers for a penny a day.

questions.question: What does Matthew 20:14 promise will happen if someone takes what is theirs and goes their way?
options: They will be given more than agreed
They will receive what they are entitled to
questions.correctAnswer: They will receive what they are entitled to
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:14 states that the householder will give unto the last even as unto the first, indicating fairness in payment.

questions.question: What is the significance of the statement, 'Is thine eye evil, because I am good'?
options: It questions the fairness of payment
It affirms the goodness of the householder
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:15 shows the householder's defense against accusations of unfairness, addressing themes of goodness and envy.

questions.question: What does Matthew 20:16 say about those who are called and chosen?
options: Many are called, but few are chosen
questions.correctAnswer: Many are called, but few are chosen
questions.explanation: This phrase in Matthew 20:16 emphasizes the difference between being called to the kingdom and being among those ultimately chosen.

questions.question: What did Jesus tell His disciples would happen to Him in Jerusalem?
options: He would be betrayed and condemned to death
He would teach in the temple
questions.correctAnswer: He would be betrayed and condemned to death
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:18 clearly states that the Son of man shall be betrayed unto the chief priests and scribes, leading to His condemnation.

questions.question: According to Matthew 20:19, what will happen on the third day after Jesus is crucified?
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:19 mentions that after being mocked, scourged, and crucified, the third day He shall rise again.

questions.question: What was the request of the mother of Zebedee's children?
options: To sit her sons on Jesus' right and left in His kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: To sit her sons on Jesus' right and left in His kingdom
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:21 indicates that she desired for her sons to have prominent positions in the kingdom.

questions.question: What did Jesus mean when He asked if the disciples could drink of the cup He would drink of?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 20:22, Jesus refers to the suffering He would endure, indicating that true discipleship involves sharing in His trials.

questions.question: What does Matthew 20:23 indicate about sitting on Jesus' right and left?
options: It is reserved for those who are faithful
It is not for Jesus to give
It is a reward for the first workers
It is promised to all believers
questions.correctAnswer: It is not for Jesus to give
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:23 clarifies that positions of honor are determined by the Father, not by Jesus' own discretion.

questions.question: How did the other ten disciples react to the request of Zebedee's children?
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:24 reveals that the other disciples were upset and indignant about the request made by Zebedee's mother.

questions.question: What lesson can be learned from the parable of the laborers in the vineyard regarding fairness?
options: God's grace is not based on human standards
All should work the same hours
Only the last workers should be rewarded
Those who complain will be punished
questions.correctAnswer: God's grace is not based on human standards
questions.explanation: The parable illustrates that God's generosity does not conform to human expectations of fairness, as shown in Matthew 20:1-16.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'the last shall be first' suggest about the Kingdom of Heaven?
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:16 highlights that the Kingdom of Heaven reverses worldly expectations, favoring humility over status.

questions.question: Is it lawful for God to do what He wills with His own?
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:15 shows that God, as the householder, has the right to do as He pleases with His own, affirming His sovereignty.

questions.question: Did the laborers who worked all day receive more than those who worked only one hour?
questions.explanation: According to Matthew 20:10-11, all workers received the same wage, which led to their murmuring, indicating unfairness by human standards.

questions.question: Did Jesus promise that everyone would be rewarded equally in His kingdom?
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:23 clarifies that rewards in the kingdom are determined by the Father, not guaranteed equally for all.

hard.title: Matthew Chapter 20 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Matthew Chapter 20.

questions.question: What did Jesus say about those who wish to be great among His followers?
questions.explanation: Jesus states in Matthew 20:26 that 'whosoever will be great among you, let him be your minister,' emphasizing humility in leadership.

questions.question: Who will be chief among Jesus' followers?
options: The one with the most followers
The one with the best education
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:27 indicates that 'whosoever will be chief among you, let him be your servant,' highlighting the principle of servant leadership.

questions.question: What did Jesus come to do according to Matthew 20:28?
options: To give his life as a ransom
questions.correctAnswer: To give his life as a ransom
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:28 specifies that Jesus 'came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many,' indicating His sacrificial mission.

questions.question: What did the two blind men cry out when Jesus passed by?
options: Have mercy on us, O Lord, thou Son of David
questions.correctAnswer: Have mercy on us, O Lord, thou Son of David
questions.explanation: In Matthew 20:30, the blind men called out, 'Have mercy on us, O Lord, thou Son of David,' recognizing Jesus' authority.

questions.question: What did the multitude do when the blind men cried out?
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:31 states that 'the multitude rebuked them,' indicating societal pressure against the blind men's cries for help.

questions.question: What was the request of the blind men to Jesus?
options: That their eyes may be opened
questions.correctAnswer: That their eyes may be opened
questions.explanation: According to Matthew 20:33, the blind men asked Jesus, 'Lord, that our eyes may be opened,' expressing their need for sight.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'diakonos' in Matthew 20:26 mean?
questions.explanation: 'Diakonos' means 'servant' in Greek, reflecting the call to serve others as a measure of greatness.

questions.question: Which literary device is primarily used in Matthew 20:26-28?
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:26-28 uses parallelism to contrast the world's view of greatness with Jesus' teaching on servanthood.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of servanthood found in Matthew 20:26-28?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 53:5 speaks of the suffering servant, which connects to Jesus' mission of serving and giving His life for others.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage connects to the concept of being a servant as mentioned in Matthew 20:26-28?
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:7 describes Jesus as taking the form of a servant, paralleling the teaching in Matthew 20 about servant leadership.

questions.question: What comes before Matthew 20:25?
options: The parable of the workers in the vineyard
The healing of the blind men
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:24 discusses the indignation of the disciples regarding the request made by the mother of Zebedee's children, which precedes verse 25.

questions.question: What does Matthew 20:16 convey about the nature of God's kingdom?
options: The first shall always be first
All will receive the same reward
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:16 states, 'So the last shall be first, and the first last,' highlighting the reversal of human expectations in God's kingdom.

questions.question: Jesus' compassion towards the blind men in Matthew 20:34 reflects what characteristic of His ministry?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 20:34, Jesus' compassion leads Him to serve the blind men by healing them, demonstrating His servant nature.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus teaches that authority is to be exercised over others in His kingdom.
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:25 shows that Jesus teaches against exercising dominion over others, instead promoting a model of servanthood.

questions.question: True or False: The blind men were quiet when Jesus passed by.
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:31 indicates that the blind men cried out even louder despite the multitude rebuking them, showing their desperation.

theological.title: Matthew Chapter 20 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Matthew Chapter 20 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Matthew 20:1 teach about the kingdom of heaven?
options: The kingdom of heaven operates on divine election beyond human merit
The kingdom of heaven is like a vineyard where all labourers receive equal pay regardless of time worked
The kingdom of heaven is a reward for exclusive early service
The kingdom of heaven is a place reserved for the righteous only
questions.correctAnswer: The kingdom of heaven is like a vineyard where all labourers receive equal pay regardless of time worked
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:1 introduces the parable illustrating the kingdom of heaven as a vineyard where labourers are hired at different times but are compensated fairly, symbolizing God's grace.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine justice is taught in Matthew 20:15?
options: God's justice is based on human works and effort
God has the sovereign right to dispense grace as He wills
God punishes those who complain about others' blessings
God rewards only those who labor the longest
questions.correctAnswer: God has the sovereign right to dispense grace as He wills
questions.explanation: In Matthew 20:15, the householder asserts his right to do what he wants with his own goods, teaching the doctrine of God's sovereign grace in dispensing mercy and reward.

questions.question: What doctrine about Jesus' mission is taught in Matthew 20:28?
options: Jesus came to be served and glorified
Jesus came to establish a political kingdom
Jesus came to give His life as a ransom for many
Jesus came to judge the nations immediately
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus came to give His life as a ransom for many
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:28 states Jesus came not to be served but to serve and give His life as a ransom, teaching the doctrine of substitutionary atonement.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Matthew 20:14 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:14 reveals God's sovereignty as the householder declares his right to give to whom he will, emphasizing God's authority over grace.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is exemplified in Jesus' compassion in Matthew 20:34?
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:34 shows Jesus moved with compassion toward the blind men, demonstrating God's merciful and caring nature.

questions.question: How does Matthew 20:17-19 connect to the broader narrative of Jesus’ passion in the New Testament?
options: It anticipates the resurrection only, without mention of suffering
It connects Jesus’ journey to Jerusalem with His foreknown suffering, death, and resurrection, fulfilling Old Testament prophecy
It focuses solely on Jesus’ teaching ministry without reference to His death
It predicts the establishment of an earthly kingdom immediately
questions.correctAnswer: It connects Jesus’ journey to Jerusalem with His foreknown suffering, death, and resurrection, fulfilling Old Testament prophecy
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:17-19 foreshadows Jesus’ passion, connecting His death and resurrection with redemptive history as foretold in Scripture.

questions.question: In what way does the parable in Matthew 20:1-16 fulfill the theme of grace in Pauline theology?
options: It teaches salvation is earned by works
It exemplifies the doctrine of justification by faith alone and God’s unmerited grace
It contradicts Paul’s teaching of predestination
It emphasizes human merit in the kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: It exemplifies the doctrine of justification by faith alone and God’s unmerited grace
questions.explanation: The parable (Matthew 20:1-16) parallels Paul’s teaching that salvation is by grace, not works, emphasizing God’s free gift to all regardless of human effort.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Matthew 20:25 and 20:26 teach about Christian leadership?
options: Christian leaders should exercise dominion like Gentile rulers
Leadership in the church requires authoritarian control
True greatness in Christian leadership is marked by servanthood and humility
Leaders must seek political power to be effective
questions.correctAnswer: True greatness in Christian leadership is marked by servanthood and humility
questions.explanation: In Matthew 20:25-26, Jesus contrasts worldly power with kingdom leadership, teaching servant leadership as the true model for believers.

questions.question: What theological insight about suffering and discipleship do Matthew 20:22 and 20:23 jointly provide?
options: Suffering is optional for Jesus’ followers
Discipleship involves sharing in Jesus’ suffering and baptism, but not guaranteed honors
The desire for status is endorsed as a mark of faith
The cup and baptism refer only to water baptism
questions.correctAnswer: Discipleship involves sharing in Jesus’ suffering and baptism, but not guaranteed honors
questions.explanation: Verses 20:22-23 teach that true discipleship includes participation in Jesus’ suffering (the cup and baptism) and that positions of honor are granted by the Father’s will, not by human request.

questions.question: What synthesis about God’s mercy and human response is taught by Matthew 20:31 and 20:34?
options: God’s mercy is only for the quiet and obedient
Persistent faith in crying out to Jesus results in compassionate healing and salvation
Human effort alone is sufficient for healing
Jesus ignores the cries of the marginalized
questions.correctAnswer: Persistent faith in crying out to Jesus results in compassionate healing and salvation
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:31 shows the blind men’s persistence despite rebuke, and 20:34 shows Jesus’ compassion responding to their faith, teaching the link between faith, persistence, and divine mercy.

questions.question: Sceptics claim the parable in Matthew 20:1-16 promotes unfairness because last hired workers receive equal pay. What does this passage actually teach?
options: God’s grace is sovereign and not dependent on human merit
God rewards people strictly according to their labor
The parable endorses human concepts of fairness over divine justice
The parable supports economic equality as the primary gospel
questions.correctAnswer: God’s grace is sovereign and not dependent on human merit
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:1-16 teaches that God’s grace is sovereign and graciously given, rather than earned by human effort, emphasizing divine generosity over human notions of fairness.

questions.question: What doctrine about Jesus’ incarnation and mission is emphasized in Matthew 20:27?
options: Jesus’ mission involves being served and glorified
Jesus’ glory is in His humility and service as a servant
Jesus is a political liberator first and foremost
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus’ glory is in His humility and service as a servant
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:27 highlights the paradox of greatness in the kingdom of God being found in humble service, reflecting Jesus’ own incarnational mission.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly displayed in the vineyard owner’s repeated calls to laborers standing idle in Matthew 20:4 and 20:7?
questions.explanation: The householder’s repeated invitation to the idle laborers (Matthew 20:4, 20:7) exemplifies God’s longsuffering patience and willingness to extend grace even late in the day.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme is prepared for by Jesus’ statement in Matthew 20:19 about rising again on the third day?
options: Fulfillment of messianic prophecy through resurrection
questions.correctAnswer: Fulfillment of messianic prophecy through resurrection
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:19 anticipates the resurrection on the third day, connecting Jesus’ death and resurrection to messianic prophecy and God’s redemptive plan.

questions.question: What doctrine regarding the nature of election and calling is taught in Matthew 20:16?
options: Many are called but few are chosen
All who are called are necessarily chosen
Only those from Israel are chosen
questions.correctAnswer: Many are called but few are chosen
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:16 states 'many be called, but few chosen,' teaching the doctrine that while the gospel call is universal, the effectual call leading to salvation is limited.
